Hi Sara / Amrit —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and a few asks so your security team has clear answers for the RFP items you called out: prompt/output storage scope, residency, and retention windows for any persisted artifacts.

Key points we covered:
- Redwood does not persist prompt inputs or model-generated outputs by default for hosted API customers unless configured (e.g., for debugging, evals, or legal retention).
- For customers who opt-in to output persistence, data can be stored in:
  * Redwood-hosted US region (multi-AZ) — default for hosted customers in North America
  * Customer-managed S3 bucket (Private / Dedicated) when using Redwood Private or Dedicated with delegated storage
  * On-prem volumes for air-gapped deployments (by contract)
- Retention: configurable TTL per customer and per route; defaults are 0 (ephemeral) for prompt payloads and 30 days for explicit persisted artifacts unless extended by contract.
- Logging/Telemetry: request metadata (time, model, token counts) are retained for operational reasons; full request/response bodies are only retained if the customer enables persistence.

Actions I promised to send:
1) A one-page retention & residency matrix showing what is stored where and for how long (attached).
2) A short blurb you can hand to your GRC team summarizing controls (access controls, KMS key options, audit logs).
3) A secured Drive link with the sample configuration for delegated S3 ingestion.

Attachments: redwood_prompt_output_retention_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet) — this has the TTL rows you asked us to pre-fill.

Next steps / asks from Lumen:
- Please confirm whether you need Redwood-hosted persistence for any PII outputs, or if you require all persisted artifacts to go to a customer-managed bucket.
- If customer-managed storage is required, provide a point of contact for S3 setup and the preferred KMS provider.

Happy to jump on a quick call with your GRC/security folks tomorrow morning if that helps.

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
1) Lumen policy requires that any persisted outputs containing PHI be stored in a customer-controlled location (S3 with our KMS). We cannot permit Redwood-hosted persistence for PHI.
2) We may allow ephemeral retention for non-PHI diagnostics for up to 72 hours only.
3) We need proof that access to persisted artifacts is limited to a named set of roles and that audit logs capture read/modify actions.

Jenny (copied) is our external security reviewer and will want the technical details and a short list of the required IAM roles for S3 ingestion.

Evelyn / Marcus —

Looping in some implementation details so we can respond to Sara and Jenny with precise language and a sample IAM policy. Notes below (first pass):

- Delegated S3 ingestion: supported in Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we can provide a private connector that writes directly to a customer S3 using temporary credentials; this is available under a dedicated contract.
- Minimal IAM permissions we recommend (S3 + KMS):
  * s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectAcl (if ACLs used), s3:ListBucket (optional for prefix validation)
  * kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey
  * kms:DescribeKey (for validation)

- Auditability: when using customer-managed S3 with KMS, access is recorded in AWS CloudTrail (customer account). On Redwood side we can additionally emit digest-level hashes and access events (no payload) into our audit logs and correlate by artifact id.
- Contract language: non-hosted residency for PHI should be called out in the SOW + Data Processing Agreement (DPA). We will need to flag that in the proposal.

Pls see the attached retention matrix (Evelyn) for the TTL defaults and per-route overrides. I'll draft the IAM snippet and a short GRC blurb and post back by EOD tomorrow.
